message.content:
{
  "summary": "Coagulant pump P-202 is delivering less than commanded, with FIT-202 at 3.02 L/h against a command of 9.15 L/h, causing clarified turbidity AIT-401 to rise to 16.9 NTU. The likely cause is crystallised PAC in the injection quill or non-return valve, worn pump check valves, a ruptured diaphragm, a blocked suction strainer, air in the pump head, or an almost empty coagulant day tank.",
  "likely_causes": [
    "Crystallised PAC in the injection quill or the non-return valve.",
    "Worn or stuck pump check valves, or a ruptured diaphragm.",
    "Suction strainer blocked, or air in the pump head.",
    "Coagulant tank nearly empty."
  ],
  "checks": [
    "Check the coagulant day tank level LIT-202 to rule out an empty tank.",
    "Check the pump stroke and the discharge pressure gauge: high pressure points to a blocked quill, low pressure to a suction or valve problem.",
    "Do a drawdown test with the calibration column to measure the real delivered flow.",
    "Look at the injection quill for white crystalline deposits."
  ],
  "handover": "Coagulant pump P-202 active flow low alarm (FIT-202 at 3.02 L/h vs command 9.15 L/h) raised at 10:30, accompanied by rising clarified turbidity AIT-401 at 16.9 NTU. Complete checks on coagulant day tank level LIT-202 (at 44.0 %), pump discharge pressure, suction strainer, and injection quill per SOP-04 before restarting or changing over to the standby pump.",
  "citations": [
    "SOP-04 4.2",
    "SOP-04 4.3",
    "SOP-04 4.4",
    "SOP-09 9.3"
  ]
}
